nodes.text: Let $a/b\in \mathbb{Q}_{>0}$ with $b$ squarefree. Are there integers $1<n_1<\cdots<n_k$, each the product of two distinct primes, such that\[\frac{a}{b}=\frac{1}{n_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n_k}?\]

#306 : [ErGr80] number theory | unit fractions For $n_i$ the product of three distinct primes, this is true when $b=1$, as proved by Butler, Erdős and Graham [BEG15] (this paper is perhaps Erdős' last paper, appearing 19 years after his death). There are several examples known of such decompositions for $a/b=1$. The first was given by Barbeau [Ba77] . The shortest known examples have $47$ terms, discovered by Watanabe [Wa20] (see the introduction of [Wa20] for further history).
